clue.text: One beginning to attend to five coming in for start of treatment

indicators.note: one thing coming in for another replaces it, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: to notice something is to attend to it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A trainee clinician is told to deal with five patients arriving for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in for' puts V where the T supplied by 'start of treatment' stood in the word for attend to.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, someone just starting out at an activity.

clue.text: Sister outside a church in shade

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, enclosing it

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun stands outside a church in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour, a slight difference.

clue.text: Handbook — copper shown in volume made me nervous

indicators.note: one piece is shown inside another, so it goes within it
nervous letters are jittery and unsettled, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder for the anagram
fodder for the anagram
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a policeman appearing in a big book rattled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' jumbles the fodder and 'shown in' places the copper symbol within the result. Copper is also slang for a police officer, the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum is a handbook or guide small enough to carry around for constant reference.

clue.text: Agree to study mould

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
to mould something is to form it

explanation.surface: Someone consents to examine a casting mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply or fall in line, which is to agree with what is expected.

clue.text: Insulating material, like finest used by sailor

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
finest means best
OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor uses the best insulating material available.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used for fireproof insulation.

clue.text: Hay fever sufferer may take one and withdraw from contest on Hampshire river

definitions.text: Hay fever sufferer may take one

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so it comes first

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw an entrant from a race or competition
the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: A competitor with hay fever pulls out of a contest held beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch test is an allergy test in which the skin is lightly scratched with possible allergens, given to hay fever patients.

clue.text: Sentiment expressed by English poet

parts.note: Andrew Motion was the British Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: An English poet voices a heartfelt sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling, and a sentiment is a feeling or attitude.

clue.text: What some northerners eat is rubbish

definitions.meaning: cow's stomach lining, traditionally eaten in the north of England

explanation.surface: A northern dish is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is both the edible stomach lining of cattle and a slang word for nonsense.

clue.text: Second place, say, could make you spit

parts.note: to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Coming second, a sore loser is so angry they could spit.
explanation.definitionFit: To splutter is to spit out saliva or food while speaking in a rush or rage.

clue.text: Fiery pit shown in painting

indicators.note: one piece shown in another sits inside it

parts.note: painting is art
a den is a pit or lair where an animal lives

explanation.surface: A painting depicts a blazing pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate or burning with feeling, a figurative sense of fiery.

clue.text: Member's spoken about one concerned with heraldry

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, surrounding it

parts.note: oral means spoken
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A club member's talk is about someone who studies coats of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a member a person in a club, but here it is a limb of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorial describes things relating to coats of arms, the subject matter of heraldry.

clue.text: Italian must go after fall? Don't be ridiculous!

indicators.note: this places one piece after the other, at the end

parts.note: to come off a horse or bike is to fall
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: An Italian has to leave after a tumble, which someone thinks is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal exclamation telling someone to stop talking nonsense, much like saying 'nonsense!'

clue.text: Banger in sack, fine specimen

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a cracker is an excellent example of something

explanation.surface: A sausage in a bag turns out to be a fine one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for a sausage, as the surface suggests, but here it is a loud firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a loud firework, and a firecracker is a firework that explodes with a bang.

clue.text: Disinclined to move from container terminal

indicators.note: the letters come from within the words that follow, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A freight hub where nothing wants to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means inactive or sluggish, lacking any urge to stir.

clue.text: Ever pinch some comic in school?

indicators.note: comic letters are made silly and jumbled up

parts.note: fodder for the anagram
fodder for the anagram
fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A question of whether anyone ever pinched a comic book at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school taking pupils of all abilities.

clue.text: Brown is one of its members, and girl attending class

definitions.text: Brown is one of its members

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name
a league is a class or level, as in out of one's league

explanation.surface: A girl called Brown goes to class with her classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is not a colour or surname here but Brown University in Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of eight elite US universities, Brown being one of them.

clue.text: Small fish and fruit

parts.note: haddock is a fish

explanation.surface: A menu offers small fish and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is a large citrus fruit, another name for the pomelo.

clue.text: Minister in PA

parts.note: being in is being at home
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A government minister works as a personal assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: PA might suggest Pennsylvania or a public address system; it is a personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Secretary is the UK government minister in charge of the Home Office.

clue.text: Sign my post, for a change, 'Mike'

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram
fodder for the anagram
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks Mike to sign the letters for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or indication, especially of an illness.

clue.text: A Latin king's listening intently

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A Latin-speaking king pays close attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for listening eagerly and attentively.

clue.text: Sound of seal and young swan

indicators.note: what follows is heard rather than written, so a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: The cry of a seal and a baby swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the standard term for a swan in its first year, still grey-feathered.

clue.text: Delight about mother coming round

indicators.note: one piece comes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed as their mother comes to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is something wonderful, a delight, as in 'it went like a dream'.

clue.text: Put up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: Something is set up ahead of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building or structure is to put it up.

clue.text: Powerful guns, not well positioned in main road

indicators.note: one piece is positioned in another, inside it

parts.note: an artery is a major road
ill means not well

explanation.surface: Heavy weapons are badly placed on a major road.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large guns used in warfare.

clue.text: Pass through stand

parts.note: over means finished, through
to take something is to stand or bear it

explanation.surface: A permit lets someone get through a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake another vehicle is to pass it.

clue.text: No good coming back after glass of beer (slang)

indicators.note: places one piece after the other

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

indicators.note: the words no and good are read backwards together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a pint of beer is no good, in slangy terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the two pieces round together, giving GON.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialised or obscure language, a near synonym of slang.

clue.text: BSI emblem, two articles surrounded by three kings

indicators.note: one piece is surrounded by another, placed inside it

parts.note: K is king in chess and R (rex) is king, giving K, R and K
an item is an article, a thing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A badge showing two objects ringed by three monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' sets the articles between the first king and the other two. BSI is the British Standards Institution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kitemark is the quality certification symbol awarded by the British Standards Institution.

clue.text: Climb a trail

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a path.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward movement.
